requirements.requirement: curl package is version-locked to its currently installed version on node1
requirements.summary: curl-7.76.1-31.el9.x86_64 was identified and a dnf versionlock entry curl-0:7.76.1-31.el9.* was added and confirmed via `dnf versionlock list`.

requirements.requirement: A subsequent system update does not change curl's version (lock is effective)
requirements.summary: A targeted `dnf update --assumeno curl` reported nothing to do, and a full dry-run system update (210 packages, 17 new installs) excluded curl itself from the transaction; only the separate libcurl package appeared, confirming the lock holds curl in place during a real update set.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered/persisted state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 15443601-... with curl version and active versionlock. Reboot was acknowledged and the node became briefly unreachable (connection reset) confirming a real disruption. Post-restart capture shows a new boot_id (a63b64e3-...), curl still at 7.76.1-31.el9, and the versionlock entry intact. This matches the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity cross-check (15443601... -> a63b64e3...).

overall_summary: The executor correctly identified curl-7.76.1-31.el9.x86_64, installed the versionlock dnf plugin, and added a versionlock pinning curl to its exact current version. It then proved the lock's effectiveness with both a targeted no-op check and a full 210-package dry-run update that excluded curl (while the separate libcurl package was still eligible, as expected). The mandatory single-node restart protocol was also completed: a healthy pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot with a brief unreachable window, a changed boot identity, and confirmation that both the curl version and the versionlock entry survived the reboot. Lifecycle snapshots show no unexplained residue, failed services, or package-health degradation beyond expected reboot artifacts.
limitations: Persistence of the lock was only verified immediately after one reboot; longer-term persistence (e.g., across a real dnf upgrade actually being run, not just a dry-run) was not tested.

The dry-run update evidence confirms curl is excluded from the transaction plan but does not execute a real update to observe post-update state, which is an acceptable and lower-risk way to demonstrate the lock without mutating 210 packages unnecessarily.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task or the mandatory restart protocol: installing dnf-command(versionlock) (cmd-efcfd37ecafd4cb0) was a necessary prerequisite; adding the versionlock (cmd-25eb5794e97d4db8) is the core task action; the dry-run updates (--assumeno) are read-only/no-op and did not mutate state; the reboot (cmd-0f5ef427de67485d) was required by the mandatory restart protocol and was bounded (single node, single restart). The lifecycle diff shows no unexpected residue beyond expected reboot artifacts (/tmp/reboot.log, new systemd-private tmp dirs tied to the new boot, changed sshd/chronyd PIDs) which are normal consequences of a reboot, not executor-caused clutter. No failed services, no damaged package state (dnf reports healthy in both snapshots), no unnecessary or unrelated mutations observed.
